For **home backup**, I’d shortlist the **Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus**: it has a 3.84 kWh battery, 6,000 W output, 120/240 V support, and up to 3,200 W solar input—useful if you need to run larger loads or recharge during a longer outage. You can pair it with compatible solar panels; check whether the listing you buy is a panel bundle, since the cited comparison doesn’t confirm panels are included. [Specs and comparison](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup)

If you mainly need **120 V essentials** like a fridge, lights, and router and want a clearly named panel pairing, the guide lists the **Anker SOLIX F3000 + PS400 panels** as an option. [Solar-generator picks by use case](https://offsetsolar.com/best/solar-generator-home-backup/)

For either setup, capacity determines how long it runs; output determines which appliances it can run at once. To connect a unit to hardwired home circuits, plan on a transfer switch or home power panel installed by an electrician—don’t backfeed through an outlet. [Backup setup guidance](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup)
